text:
nate: Heads up — MediLedger (healthcare data partner) wants a 9-month commit. They want guidance on reserved GPUs, burst strategy, and answers for their security questionnaire. Their recap: baseline ~3k req/min, predictable daily spike to 9k req/min for ~20 minutes, avg response ~16 tokens. p95 target 300ms. Can we size and give a short preheat/playbook?

claire: Quick clarify — is that 9k req/min = 150 req/s? that maps to tokens/sec ~2400 (150*16). We should convert to token throughput per GPU.

ram: Performance baseline (for our quantized-medium on A100-class): ~550 tokens/sec per GPU sustained w/o batching. With efficient batching and short responses we often see effective throughput 2.5x, but use conservative 1.8x for sizing => ~1000 tokens/sec per GPU. So 2400 tokens/sec peak -> ~3 GPUs. But factor in redundancy, rolling updates, and cooling headroom -> recommend 6 reserved GPUs + 3 burst credits.

maya: Short autoscale & preheat proposal (paste into RFP):
```yaml
autoscale:
  reserved_replicas: 6
  burst_credit_pool: 3
  min_replicas: 6
  max_replicas: 14
  target_tokens_per_gpu: 1000
  scale_up_window_s: 45
  scale_down_window_s: 180
  scale_policy: prefer_reserved_then_burst
preheat:
  method: kv_prefix_and_synthetic
  kv_prefixes: ["/session/*","/user/*"]
  kv_warm_duration_s: 1200
  synthetic_ramp_s: 300
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 48
  max_latency_ms: 35
fallback:
  model_variant: gpt-medium-quant-8bit
```
Notes: freeze scale-down for 30m around expected spike windows and ensure KV warm keys are provided by customer (top 1k session hashes).

nate: Good. Add a line for provisioning lag so sales can set expectations.

ram: Provisioning notes: attaching and warming a dedicated GPU replica ~8-12 minutes; burst spot instances usually available ~2-6 minutes depending on region. KV warm may take 5-15 minutes to reach steady-state depending on hit rate. Recommend customer schedule preheat 20 minutes before expected peak.

sales-ops: Pricing sketch: offer 9-month reserved commit for 6 GPUs with 15% discount vs on-demand, include 3 burst credits/month (each credit = 1 GPU-minute at burst spec). HSM/KMS + extended logs are billable extras. Will draft quote.

security: From their questionnaire: CMK support, option for HSM, audit export to customer S3, retention SLA (they want 13 months). We can support CMK and S3 export; 13 months retention is enterprise add-on. HSM available as managed add-on (+~3% infra). Provide SOC2 and penetration test summary.

nate: Can someone paste a tiny runbook for them to run in their VPC to validate performance during POC? Need a load command, preheat call, and emergency fallback steps.

maya: Runbook snippet for ticket: 
```bash
# sample vegeta target file (warm small messages)
echo 'POST https://dedicated-ml.redwood/v1/generate\nContent-Type: application/json\nAuthorization: Bearer $TOKEN\n\n{"prompt":"keepalive","max_tokens":12}' > targets.txt
vegeta attack -targets=targets.txt -rate=150 -duration=20m | vegeta report

# server-side KV preheat
redwoodctl preheat --project mediledger --prefix "/session/*" --duration 1200

# emergency fallback commands
redwoodctl failover --project mediledger --variant gpt-medium-quant-8bit
redwoodctl enable-burst --project mediledger --credits 3
```
Replace endpoint with tenant-specific VPC host.

claire: Failure modes to call out (short bullets for runbook): cache-miss storm -> use rate limiter + synthetic ramp; sustained >85% token_util -> trigger on-call and enable burst; sudden provisioning lag -> degrade to smaller model variant and shed low-priority jobs.

ops-bot: ops-bot: preheat job queued mediledger-preheat-2410001410 by maya

security: I'll attach SOC2 pdf + KMS integration guide in the ticket and note rotation policies (we support 30/90/365 day key rotation cadence). Also confirm export encryption in transit to their S3.

nate: OK next steps: sales-ops send quote + line items, security attaches docs, ops schedule preheat window post-sign, and engineering confirm that the model variant fallback is tested. Ping back here if MediLedger provides historical traffic samples. Thanks :thumbsup:
